name: Overlay Readability And Focus Stack
use_when: Text, arrows, screenshots, lower thirds, or graphics need to clarify what the viewer should notice.
The original footage is busy and the agent needs to direct attention.
An overlay should cover a jump cut, introduce a speaker, or explain a proof point.
A short-form visual stack uses text, icons, stock footage, or GIFs to show the spoken concept.
A dense After Effects Reel needs overlays, captions, animated text, and transition covers to clear cleanly between segments.
Texture overlays, light leaks, dust, electric effects, or screen-blend accents are being used as highlights or transitions.
Document highlights, map markers, route arrows, chart labels, or screenshot focus strips need clear hierarchy.
Text must be placed in negative space or integrated into a live-action frame without hiding the subject.
avoid_when: The overlay repeats what is already visually obvious.
The screen already has too many competing text or graphic layers.
The overlay would cover the face, action, title, product, map, or evidence.

timeline_pattern.focus_rule: Only one element should be the primary focus at a time.
timeline_pattern.readability_rule: Use stroke, drop shadow, background box, blur, or dimming when footage makes text hard to read.
timeline_pattern.cleanup_rule: Remove overlays before the next focal point unless they remain necessary context.
timeline_pattern.visualization_rule: If on-screen text or an icon already carries the concept, reduce duplicate captions or lower-priority text.
timeline_pattern.out_animation_rule: When no motivated overlay transition covers the change, slide, fade, or otherwise clear elements so they do not disappear harshly.
timeline_pattern.texture_rule: Screen-blend texture overlays need a named highlight, transition, or mood job and should be trimmed to the beat.
timeline_pattern.evidence_rule: When overlays point to evidence, they must reveal and preserve the source detail rather than covering it.
timeline_pattern.typography_rule: Use font weight, size, case, and color to create one primary focus instead of stacking multiple equal text layers.
timeline_pattern.negative_space_rule: Prefer unused frame space for overlay text; do not place text over the emotional or evidentiary focal point.

motion.rule: Keep overlay motion short and functional; do not animate every label if it slows comprehension.

keyframe_values.overlay_in_duration: 4-8 frames for pop-in social emphasis; 8-16 frames for calmer explainers.
keyframe_values.background_dim: Start around 20-45% opacity when the footage competes with the overlay.
keyframe_values.blur_radius: Use only enough blur to separate the overlay; avoid hiding evidence.
keyframe_values.safe_margin: Keep critical text inside platform safe margins and away from captions.
keyframe_values.out_animation: Use short fades or slide-outs before the next visual stack when elements would otherwise pop off abruptly.
keyframe_values.document_highlight: Use a wipe or mask reveal for source highlights, then hold long enough to read the wording.
keyframe_values.map_arrow: Route arrows should travel in the direction the viewer should understand.
keyframe_values.typography_hierarchy: One impact word or phrase should dominate when overlay text is more than a label.

sound.rule: Use subtle ticks or hits only for overlays that mark a real beat; avoid repetitive whooshes for every graphic.
sound.infographic_note: Use marker, shutter, or highlight cues only on major evidence reveals.

captions.rule: Captions, lower thirds, and overlays must be laid out together so they do not collide.

color.rule: Choose overlay color and contrast for readability over both bright and dark footage. Tint or lower texture overlays so they fit the palette and do not create compression dirt.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use drawtext, overlay, box, shadow, fade, and optional background blur/dim layers; generate contact sheets at delivery size for collisions.
implementation.remotion: Create overlay components with safe-area props, z-index rules, text shadow/stroke styles, and collision checks against caption regions.
implementation.blender: Use text objects, arrows, or planes with restrained animation for callouts in composited sequences.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use text stroke, shadow, background style, canvas blur/dim, stickers/arrows, and manual layer timing.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics, Drop Shadow, Stroke, Gaussian Blur on duplicated background layers, guide overlays, and Screen/Add blend modes for black-background texture overlays. In After Effects, trim overlay layers by segment, use out animations or motivated overlay transitions, and suppress captions where animated text already carries the line.

common_mistakes: Stacking captions, title text, card text, and arrows until the viewer has no clear focus.
Using a transparent image or green-screen overlay without checking edges and timing.
Leaving an overlay onscreen after its spoken reference has passed.
Covering the title or main proof point in a short-form layout.
Showing every spoken word as overlay text when a simple icon, stock shot, or visual proof would communicate faster.
Letting elements vanish between After Effects segments without an out animation or transition cover.
Leaving texture overlays over captions, faces, or proof after their highlight beat has passed.
Putting a highlight or marker over the exact map label, document text, or chart value the viewer needs to inspect.
Using shadow, gradient, or blend mode as decoration when plain contrast would read faster.
qc: Is there only one primary on-screen focus at each moment?
Is all text readable at phone size?
Do captions, lower thirds, and overlays avoid collisions?
Does the overlay clear before it competes with the next beat?
Does background dim or blur preserve the evidence the viewer still needs?
Do duplicate captions or overlays get removed when the visual stack already explains the idea?
Do dense AE overlays clear with an out animation or motivated transition before the next segment?
Does every texture overlay have a named job and preserve caption/proof readability?
Do document highlights, map arrows, and chart overlays reveal evidence without hiding it?
Does overlay typography have one clear primary focus and a clean negative-space placement?
